Architecture / owner boundaries / planning baseline

The strict architecture standard is not yet met.

The codebase contains useful independent components, but the migration remains incomplete. Competing policy paths, concrete storage dependencies and uneven enforcement still prevent the whole application from meeting its intended standard.

The architectural conclusion

A stronger foundation, with unfinished boundaries.

The remaining work is concentrated in ownership, contracts and adoption. Extracted libraries do not yet make every application boundary independently defensible.

Durable confirmation still has parallel interpreters. Study orchestration reaches global stores and persistence layouts. Some adapters expose physical database representations, while the selected ownership checks and shared CI mapping cover less than the intended architecture.

FE001 FE003 FE005 ST005 RT002 RT004

How to use this review

Plan against the precise failure, including its limits.

A confirmed item establishes the stated source-level mismatch; it does not claim a reproduced production incident. A candidate requires an owner decision or stronger reachability/contract evidence before implementation.

Separate adapters, deliberate pure replicas and retained compatibility can be legitimate. The registry records counterevidence so that consolidation preserves required behavior and avoids unnecessary abstractions.

BE006 FE009 FE012 FE013

Priorities are proposed planning urgency. Assignees, implementation evidence and accepted commitments remain open.

Preserve and extend

Interfaces that already provide a useful foundation

These are positive examples and reusable owners. Their existence should guide the next steps; it does not clear every caller or prove complete production adoption.

✓

A reusable durable session

@tempo/study-session

Explicit IntentStore and LearningClient capabilities already separate durable submission, settlement and bounded next loading from React and application stores.

Public contract and qualification ↗ FE003 FE006

✓

A renderer-neutral board contract

@tempo/board-ui

Plain presentation values, events and a narrow imperative handle have package-local and installed-consumer qualification. Application adoption remains incomplete.

Public contract and qualification ↗ FE002

✓

Shared pure scheduling and identity

tempo_scheduling · tempo_chess_core

The scheduling kernel and identity owner are extracted; compatibility wrappers can delegate rather than fork algorithms. Cross-runtime identity parity is explicit.

Public contract and qualification ↗ BE006 FE012 FE013

✓

Independent evidence mathematics

tempo_evidence_math

Pure evidence arithmetic, reach, readiness and valuation have a public package and independent qualification. Source purity does not by itself prove every consuming boundary.

Public contract and qualification ↗ BE004 BE014

✓

Detached Game Review contracts

tempo_game_review_contracts

Shared values and capability protocols permit independently constructed ingestion and comparison. Distinct workflows still need clear authority and adoption.

Public contract and qualification ↗ BE005

✓

An injected browser intent store

@tempo/browser-intents

A typed factory/store capability already exists below application-specific browser journals. It provides a concrete model for reducing reverse application dependencies.

Public contract and qualification ↗ ST003 FE005

Proposed implementation sequence

Organize the work around owners

Start with durable confirmation and trustworthy boundary/proof maps, then extract application contracts. Preserve retained work during consolidation. Board work can proceed independently; evidence and current documentation should improve with every change.

01
Operation receipts and Study time

Protect original identities and unify confirmation semantics.

Repair receipt interpretation and Study-day calculation before larger extraction. Keep each durable journal under its proper owner.

3 findings · 2 P1 · 0 candidates

02
Owner map and qualification selection

Make the declared architecture match the code that runs.

Update the existing owner/export maps and qualification selection. Defend actual public boundaries and keep native proof where persistence effects require it.

3 findings · 1 P1 · 0 candidates

03
Study application and persistence contracts

Move orchestration behind semantic capabilities.

Replace storage-shaped inputs, global assembly and private implementation dependencies with explicit application and transaction contracts.

21 findings · 2 P1 · 0 candidates

04
Shared domain policies and retired paths

Choose one supported owner for each rule.

Separate live duplication from retained compatibility. Consolidate duplicated invariants, preserve retained work, and decide candidates before implementation.

19 findings · 0 P1 · 4 candidates

05
Shared board presentation

Use one renderer with separate application policies.

Adopt the independent board contract while preserving Study-specific legality, sound, hints, keyboard behavior and persistent ownership.

1 findings · 0 P1 · 0 candidates

06
Proof and current documentation

Keep evidence and current guidance aligned with the result.

Repair misleading or stale proof paths, update the current catalogs and document remaining limits. Re-run affected checks as each owner changes.

8 findings · 4 P1 · 0 candidates

Scope
Published main source at 40172873, including the merged tactic-admission repair PR987. The initial full review at fede1da7 was reconciled against all seven changed files and the new complete tree. All 2,760 unchanged blobs match. No live installation or database was inspected; source-level repair review does not establish installed acceptance.
Standard
Strict modular-monolith goals and current AGENTS.md component/transaction/testing rules. A function or dataclass can be a valid interface. Facades, adapters, cross-runtime replicas and historical migrations are not automatically violations.
Confirmed finding
The stated source-level architectural mismatch is evidenced. Confirmed does not mean a production failure was reproduced.
Candidate
The source pattern is evidenced, but whether it violates the intended boundary depends on an explicit owner/support decision or additional reachability/contract proof.
Priority
P1: current invariants, retained identities, or trustworthy verification need early attention. P2: core consolidation/interface independence. P3: bounded retained-path, documentation or portability work. These are proposed planning priorities, not production incident severities.
Semantic review
Relevant responsibilities, interface data/effects and source consumers were reviewed. This does not imply every runtime branch was exercised or every line proven correct.
Structural review
Static source/import/definition/SQL or configuration checks were performed. No finding in this level is not an architectural compliance certificate.
Inventory review
The tracked path, category and source identity were recorded. Assets/lockfiles and some documentation/fixtures were not semantically reviewed.
Static limits
Python AST edges include deferred/type-only imports. JavaScript/TypeScript edges are literal scans, not compiler-resolved. Cycles, clone searches and table-writer counts are review leads rather than automatic failures.
Planning state
Open and Needs decision are audit classifications. Proposed workstreams and recommendations are not accepted implementation commitments. Assignee and PR/evidence fields are intentionally blank.
